modern: The sun seems to be poured down, and indeed it is spread in all directions, yet it is not poured out. For this spreading is extension: so its rays are called Extensions because they are extended. And one may judge what kind of thing a ray is if he looks at the sun’s light passing through a narrow opening into a darkened room, for it is extended in a straight line, and is, as it were, divided when it meets any solid body which stands in the way and cuts off the air beyond; but there the light stays fixed and does not slide or fall off. Such, then, ought to be the pouring out and spreading of the understanding: it should in no way be a pouring away, but an extension, and it should make no violent or headlong collision with the obstacles in its way; nor yet fall down, but be fixed, and light up what receives it. For a body will deprive itself of the light if it does not let it in.
original: The sun appears to be poured down, and in all directions indeed it is diffused, yet it is not effused. For this diffusion is extension: Accordingly its rays are called Extensions because they are extended. But one may judge what kind of a thing a ray is, if he looks at the sun’s light passing through a narrow opening into a darkened room, for it is extended in a right line, and as it were is divided when it meets with any solid body which stands in the way and intercepts the air beyond; but there the light remains fixed and does not glide or fall off. Such then ought to be the outpouring and diffusion of the understanding, and it should in no way be an effusion, but an extension, and it should make no violent or impetuous collision with the obstacles which are in its way; nor yet fall down, but be fixed, and enlighten that which receives it. For a body will deprive itself of the illumination, if it does not admit it.
